name: Molmo (pointing)
summary: Molmo is trained on human-collected pointing annotations alongside dense captions, giving it the ability to answer spatial questions by emitting image coordinates rather than prose. That single capability makes it directly useful as a manipulation front-end: 'point at the handle you would grasp' is a query a robot can consume, and the weights and data are fully open.
innovation: Pointing as a trained output modality, producing grounded coordinates instead of ambiguous text.
Fully open model, data and training recipe at a time when competitive VLMs were closed.
matters: Became a common open grounding module inside robot systems needing 'where', not just 'what'.
limits: 2D image points only, so depth and 3D pose must come from elsewhere.
lineage: CLIP-lineage vision-language modeling specialized toward spatial grounding for embodied use.
